chains.title: FOXA1-dependent enhancer effect on TOX3
chains.element: EH38E3180851, a distal enhancer-like element overlapping rs4784227

links.claim: This hypothesis provisionally predicts that FOXA1 binds ref C more strongly than alt T; FOXA1 occupies the site and is abundant in MCF-7, but no supplied evidence measures allele-specific binding or provides a QBiC-SELEX result establishing this direction.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851, but allele-dependent activity or FOXA1 dependence has not been demonstrated.
TOX3 is the leading candidate target by proximity and genetic prioritization, but this cCRE has not been directly linked to TOX3; no significant GTEx eQTL is reported.
FOXA1 occupancy and high expression make MCF-7 a plausible context for this proposed mechanism.
Alt T is associated with breast cancer risk, and TOX3 has gene-level breast cancer support, but the evidence does not connect FOXA1 binding at this element to TOX3 regulation or risk.

predictions: In allele-specific FOXA1 occupancy assays in MCF-7, C should show greater occupancy than T; this is a proposed direction, not an observed result.
If FOXA1 mediates the variant effect, FOXA1 perturbation should reduce the allele-dependent enhancer or TOX3 response. The direction of the TOX3 response is not established by the supplied evidence.
falsified_if: A well-powered allele-specific assay shows equal FOXA1 occupancy or greater occupancy on T.
FOXA1 perturbation has no allele-dependent effect on enhancer output or TOX3 expression.

outcomes.outcome: Perturbation changes enhancer activity and TOX3 expression; a FOXA1-dependent component is expected, but its direction is not established.

matrix.test: Precisely edit C to T and T to C in an isogenic MCF-7 model; measure candidate-TF occupancy, enhancer output, and TOX3 expression.

outcomes.outcome: The edit changes FOXA1 occupancy in the predicted C-greater-than-T direction and produces an allele-dependent enhancer or TOX3 response.
The edit changes GATA3 occupancy in the predicted T-greater-than-C direction and produces an allele-dependent enhancer or TOX3 response.
The edit changes SPDEF occupancy in the predicted T-greater-than-C direction and produces an allele-dependent enhancer or TOX3 response.

next_experiment: The cheapest experiment that separates the two highest-probability chains is allele-specific FOXA1 and GATA3 occupancy measurement at rs4784227 in MCF-7 (targeted ChIP-qPCR or CUT&RUN with allele-aware readout). H1 predicts greater FOXA1 occupancy on C; H2 predicts greater GATA3 occupancy on T. Neither direction is established by current evidence.

Key examples include promoter mutations [e.g., rs2279744 (Mouse double minute 2 homolog gene; MDM2)], enhancer mutations [e.g., rs4784227 (thymocyte selection-associated high mobility group box family member 3 gene; TOX3)], and lncRNAs [e.g., HOX transcript antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR)] linked to progression, metastasis, and poor survival.

ObjectiveAlthough several studies have identified an association between the rs4784227-cancer susceptibility candidate gene 16 (CASC16) polymorphism and breast cancer, the results remain inconclusive.

Our pooled analysis showed a significant association between the rs4784227- (T) allele and breast cancer susceptibility in Asian and North American populations, and intervention with this mutation might be a new therapeutic strategy for breast cancer.
